starting_state: 3-Feb T24 regional combat-serviceable 39-49 centered 44 with fragmented C/C- eastern-node C2.

regional_air.interpretation: Runway-based mass strike capability is nearly exhausted, but distributed water/recon assets and a few fighters still preserve warning/harassment functions.

sensor_C2.Roi_Kwajalein_primary_radar: Primary exposed antennas are destroyed or intermittent centered after repeated 4-5 Feb reattack. Do not credit A-grade pre-battle warning performance at H-hour.
sensor_C2.surviving_network: Protected plot fragments, alternate power, buried/alternate telephone, visual posts, DF/radio and outer-atoll/water-air reports survive unevenly.
sensor_C2.warning_effect: General assault warning and shelter/manning orders survive; precise fighter vectoring and continuous island-wide picture do not.

AA_and_fire_control.note: Branch radar/AA gains appear mainly as crew survival, calibration, protected power/plot and faster remanning. Exposed guns and antennas are still vulnerable to repeated naval/air attack.

base_system.aircraft_revetment_effect: Reduces correlated aircraft/mechanic/spares loss; does not protect from direct hits.
base_system.fuel_ammo: Distributed stocks prevent total one-hit loss, but local access is increasingly fragmented by bombardment and crater/debris fields.
base_system.repair: Night repair teams restore limited runway/taxi use repeatedly, but daytime reattack prevents return to high-output operations.

anti_double_count: Do not add a separate radar bonus to aircraft already preserved by the hardening/alert model.
Do not treat surviving water-air as extra land-based strike aircraft.
Do not interpret physically fireable AA as simultaneously controlled/observed AA.
